response: Prompting primary care providers about increased patient risk as a result of family history does not appear to be effective on its own. According to the available data, simple, at-the-visit family history prompts did not lead to any significant improvement in primary care providers' ability to identify patients at high risk for common conditions. Further studies are needed to examine physicians' perception of the utility of prompts for family history risk and to explore alternative methods for effectively utilizing family history information to identify high-risk patients.
